newsitem.title: USA: USDA issues revised final rule on "fresh" poultry.
newsitem.headline: USDA issues revised final rule on "fresh" poultry.

text.p: The Agriculture Department Tuesday published a revised final rule on poultry labeling to meet with legislation passed by Congress.
The poultry regulations, issued by USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS), bar the use of the term "fresh" on birds that have been cooled below 26 degrees F.
In a notice in the Federal Register, FSIS said poultry whose temperature has dropped below 26 degrees but above zero degrees was not required to bear any specific labeling.
But poultry cooled at or below zero degrees F. would be labelled "frozen" or "previously frozen," it said.
Originally, the department sought to term poultry that had cooled to less than 26 degrees but more than zero degrees as "hard chilled" or "previously hard chilled."
The labeling rules go into effect December 17, 1997.
